correctness.rationale: For the repaired claim, solving p d[k+1]−q d[k]=1/n with zero total increment and then imposing zero mean gives the kernel, including the deterministic case with r⁰=1; at zero bias the second difference is 2/n off the source. Circulant row/column absolute sums coincide. The row signs attain ℓ∞; a unit point mass attains ℓ¹. In the frozen claim a counterexample is n=3, ε=0: G=(2/3)(I−J), both norms are 8/9, and the best ℓ¹ ratio of a full sign vector is only 16/27. Increasing successive differences give one negative block. On Fourier modes, n²λ tends to 2π²m²−2πiβm and inverse coefficients are uniformly bounded by 1/(8m²), giving uniform kernel convergence at mesh points and then the Riemann sum. The displayed continuum kernel has matching endpoints, jump −2 in its derivative and zero mean, so gives precisely that inverse. By mean zero its absolute integral is twice the negative mass. The exponential and constant errors each have L¹ mass 1/(2β²). In the finite strong-drift regime the centered ramp has absolute sum n/(4ε) for even n and (n−1/n)/(4ε) for odd n, and the other two terms each have absolute sum p/ε², giving the finite bound and sharp limit.
residual_risks: The norms are full-space counting norms; a mean-zero-input optimization is not claimed. No inhomogeneous or non-nearest-neighbor case is claimed.
